texts.facts: The Opposite Party had mortgaged the aforesaid land and building along with another plot of land in favour of the Central Bank of India against a loan amount of Rs.10.35 crores including T.L./C.C. & B.G. However, subsequently, due to financial problem caused by loss in business, the Opposite Party was unable to liquidate its outstanding loan liabilities towards the Central Bank of India and TATA Capital Financial Services Ltd. and accordingly the loan at Central Bank had been classified as NPA and the property of the Opposite Party had been attached by the said bank. 8. The Opposite Party had approached the Applicant and made an offer to sell the aforesaid plot of land measuring 2 Katha 10 Lechas along with the RCC building to the Applicant in order to clear its outstanding loan amount at Central Bank of India and TATA Capital Financial Services Ltd. However, in-spite of the aforesaid payments and in-spite of several verbal requests made by the Applicant, the Opposite Party failed to execute the registered sale deed in favour of the Applicant thereby violating the terms of the agreement for sale dated 29.08.2017. Subsequent to the execution of the agreement for sale dated 29.08.2017 and after taking possession on September, 2017 the Applicant has been regularly paying the tax in respect to the said Smt. Anjana Bora vs Sankardev Commercial Pvt Ltd And Ors on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118474161/ 6 property to the GMC. Accordingly, the Applicant applied to the relevant authorities for grant of trade license/NOC for "IMFL 'ON' Bar cum Restaurant". The GMC on being satisfied issued the NOC dated 20.02.2024 whereby it allowed the Applicant to operate the trade of "IMFL 'ON' Bar cum Restaurant" in the name & style of "M/s Krib" at the ground floor of Hotel Apollo Grand
texts.arguments: The Applicant had cleared all outstanding payments of the Opposite Party against the loans and accordingly has been in possession of the property. Thereafter, left with no other option, the Applicant paid the amount of Rs.4,38,853/- to the GMC which ought to have been paid by the Opposite Party as it pertained to the years prior to the agreement for sale dated 29.08.2017 and the same was not a part of the said agreement. Moreover, pursuant to the agreement for sale dated 29.08.2017 the said property has been under the possession of the Smt. Anjana Bora vs Sankardev Commercial Pvt Ltd And Ors on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118474161/ 7 Applicant since September, 2017 and it has been duly agreed between both parties that the Applicant may run any business in the said property when the said property is under the possession of the Applicant. Hence, the Opposite Party ought to have immediately entered into a sale deed and proceeded for registration of the property in favour of the Applicant. Infact the Applicant is in possession of the property as agreed in the agreement for sale dated 29.08.2017 and ought to be the rightful owner of the said property on today's date. This Hon'ble Court under misrepresentation of facts passed an interim order on 15.03.2024 to not to pass any final order of the trade license to the Applicant without taking leave of this Hon'ble Court. 16. Mr. K.N. Choudhury, learned Senior Counsel submits that it is trite law that the party who invokes the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court under Article 226 of the Constitution is Smt. Anjana Bora vs Sankardev Commercial Pvt Ltd And Ors on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118474161/ 8 supposed to be truthful and disclose all material facts without any reservation even if such facts are against him. In other words, the Opposite Party cannot play hide and seek or pick and choose the facts he likes to disclose and to suppress or not to disclose other facts which are not in his favour. As the Opposite Party has suppressed material fact so as to obtain a favourable order from this Hon'ble Court, it is not entitled to any equitable relief from this Hon'ble Court and accordingly the interim order dated 15.03.2024 needs to be vacated. It is, therefore, of utmost necessity that the petitioner approaching the Writ Court must come with clean hands, put forward all the facts before the Court without concealing or suppressing anything and seek an appropriate relief. If there is no candid disclosure of relevant and material facts or the petitioner is guilty of misleading the Court, his petition may be dismissed at the threshold without considering the merits of the claim. 19. E converso, Mr. D. Saraf, learned counsel for the opposite party/writ petitioner, while opposing the application, submits that the Applicant is the proprietor of M/s. Satyam Associates and M/S Krib and the Applicant is carrying on/intends to carry on business under the same name from the property of the Opposite Party, the same is in utter violation of clause 7 of the agreement dated 29/08/2017 in as much as the Applicant was permitted to run business from the property of the Opposite Party only on the condition that the Opposite Party shall have a share in the proposed business and the share percentage will be decided amicably by both parties. The Applicant has failed to comply with the said condition and still intends to carry on business from the property of the Opposite Party as a proprietor which is in violation of agreement dated 29/08/2017 under which the Applicant is claiming rights.
